title: v39.0.0-beta.3 resizability broken with transparent window
body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

39.0.0-beta.3

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

10

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

39.0.0-beta.2

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

Window should be transparent and resizable if created as transparent and resizable

### Actual Behavior

both win11 and win10, resizing does no longer work if the window is transparent

This most likely was caused by: https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/48378

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/reporter/df9af8f7024137dfaf59de3e7b8909bc

### Additional Information

the gist is from this issue I created: https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/48421
please check the issue for additional information, testing can be done the same way

Related issue for transparency being broken in win10: https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/48592

comments.body:
One other thing to add because there is discussion about themes and reproducibility here.  There is a long standing issue with `transparent: true`, `frame: false` windows when the root `html` element is fully transparent (CSS) and has some margin.  But this only affects Windows 10 & 11 and then only for some HW/SW combinations.  As best I could ascertain it's mostly affecting GPU compositing enabled machines using NVIDIA GPUs/drivers.

This is of course a separate issue as it's been around for several years at a minimum, but it might be affecting the test-ability of this issue for some devs.

And finally the hack/workaround that I use to "fix" this is applying a background-color that is very nearly transparent but not fully, a. la., `html {background-color: rgb(127 127 127 / 0.002)}`.  My test video is one such window using this technique.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
@participant2 
I looked into it, and this seems to be an upstream issue. refer to https://github.com/electron/electron/compare/v39.0.0-alpha.5...v39.0.0-alpha.6.

Note that in previous versions, you needed `{frame: false, transparent: true}` to display a transparent window correctly. In `v39.0.0-alpha.5`, it restores normally, but in `v39.0.0-alpha.6`, after restoring, the background becomes white.

I tested `v39.0.0-beta.3` on a `Windows 10 22H2` virtual machine, and it works consistently. In non-virtual environments, this issue occurs in all versions after `v39.0.0-alpha.5`.

Sorry, if the issue cannot be reproduced in a virtual environment, I won’t be able to investigate it because I don’t have the necessary hardware to do so.🤯

comments.author: participant1

comments.body:
@participant1 This seems to be correct as the Electron docu also mentions that a transparent window might not be resizable on some systems (https://<redacted-host>/docs/latest/tutorial/custom-window-styles#limitations) but I don't think we should break this functionality as it would impact a lot of users.

The original bug for which the pull request was made (https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/48352) specifically references setResizable(true).
If the fix is to remove resizability as a functionality, does it even make sense to have the code change at all?

At least creating a resizable transparent window was still possible which means that users who do not need to change resizability would be able to use this, additionally a possible workaround would have been to set the min and max sizes to the same value to prevent resizing and later adapt it to re-enable resizing or vice versa.

I think breaking this would cause a lot of noise without any clear upsides.
Personally I do not need this for any of my projects so I am not biased on either decision but I think this should be discussed.
@participant2 Any opinions from the electron team on how this should be approached?

Also to note `thickFrame` is a property which can be set for a browserWindow on creation (https://<redacted-host>/docs/latest/api/structures/base-window-options), maybe this can be utilized? I.e. add a setThickFrame function for devs to toggle the window style and be able to change the electron internal state. (probably a stretch but could be used as a 'hack' for devs)

I just noticed another very important change that happened
In the newer version creating a transparent, resizable window and checking the **`window.resizable`** flag gives **`false`**

```

console.log(mainWindow.resizable);
=> false
```

Another spooky breaking change that is not intuitive for developers

As shown in my [gist](https://gist.github.com/participant5/76819a70858cb873b12c80ee63696194) from [this duplicate issue](https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/48576), the same problem (the window not being resizable) occurs when `thickFrame` is set to false as of Electron v38.3.0.

---

I suspect https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/48378 and https://github.com/electron/electron/commit/2af34b7353ac83d4aed020788e192652e0cf3ed6:

> This brings two changes that need to be confirmed.: one is that windows with thickFrame: false can no longer get the maximize button unless implemented manually. **The other is that when thickFrame is false, isResizable is always false** under normal circumstances.

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
@participant2 I was able to confirm that this naive patch fixes resize for `transparent:true`.

```patch
diff --git a/shell/browser/native_window_views.cc b/shell/browser/native_window_views.cc
index 05e40ed631..bbf8fce28a 100644
--- a/shell/browser/native_window_views.cc
+++ b/shell/browser/native_window_views.cc
@@ -1008,7 +1008,7 @@ void NativeWindowViews::MoveTop() {

 bool NativeWindowViews::CanResize() const {
 #if BUILDFLAG(IS_WIN)
-  return resizable_ && thick_frame_;
+  return resizable_;
 #else
   return resizable_;
 #endif
```

I can further confirm that using `BrowserWindow({thickFrame: true})` is insufficient to restore resize.  I don't know, yet, if that's because it is not getting associated with the internal `thick_frame_` flag or if `resizable_` is still being set to false. I'll look into that next.

However, I'm concerned that there is some sort of philosophical conflict happening here.  I was re-reading @participant1 's comments from #48378 and there seems to be a suggestion that resizing transparent windows on win32 platforms required thickFrame..

> "Note: In previous versions, transparent windows did not support resizing by dragging the borders."

This above statement in particular is false and/or incomplete.  Of course many of us have been resizing `frame:false` && `transparent:false` windows for years before that pull-request.

Because I'm not sure what the intention of coupling resizability with thick-frame originally was in PR #48378 I'm not exactly sure what the correct fix would be.

 1. If there is a compelling argument for coupling resize with thick-frame, then I suppose the fix would be to track down why the internal `thick_frame_` flag is not responding to the corresponding `BrowserWindwow({thickFrame:true})` option; or why the `resizable_` internal value is stuck as false (see above comments about root cause unidentified as-of-yet).
 2. If we disavow the notation that resizing is coupled with thick-frame on win32, then I don't see any reasons for why the above naive patch, or some other variant of it, would not make everyone happy.

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
Follow up to https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/48554#issuecomment-3725640392

The reason `thick_frame_` can't be true, in the context of this issue, is due to `NativeWindowViews` checking for `transparent:true` and forcing `thick_frame_` to false.

Ref:
https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/5901d8a6d8bf019bf8b535cb8ffe18860bdf3ad3/shell/browser/native_window_views.cc#L212-L215

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
I'm educating myself on `WS_THICKFRAME` and I think some of my confusion (and possibly some confusion in the `native_window_views.cc` code too, comes from the poor naming of this flag.  It has an alias of `WS_SIZEBOX` and dictates if a window can be resized or not.  As far as I can tell it has little or nothing to do with a visual frame, and should be entirely managed with the electron `resizable` option.  It seems that setting `thickFrame:true` also removes the `WM_CAPTION` flag as means to remove shadows?  I suppose if it works, then great, but it's not documented as such..

> WS_CAPTION	0x00C00000L	The window has a title bar (includes the WS_BORDER style).

Cit: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/winmsg/window-styles
> WS_THICKFRAME	0x00040000L	The window has a sizing border. Same as the WS_SIZEBOX style.

Now comes the curious part; when looking at pre-#48554 I still see the same `if (transparent()) thick_frame_ = false`.  And following that assignment there is a block for handling `!has_frame()`...

https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/08b7a1f801c15dbeb0acdf67a326d17ee1b6144d/shell/browser/native_window_views.cc#L368-L387

That block should remove the `WS_THICKFRAME` flag rendering the window un-resizable during construction.

The new question is, why if `thick_frame_` was always being set to false, in both older and current versions of electron, did `transparent:false` & `frame:false` & `thickFrame:true` BrowserWindows support resizing in (pre-#48554)?

We can see that the post-#48554 code has a more correct CanResize() that includes the check for `thick_frame_`, but the window itself should not have the `WS_THICKFRAME` flag in both old and new code.  Somehow that flag is sneaking in for old builds, but how?

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
@participant3 
I believe this is a conflict between the design goals and the actual behavior. From the logic of the code, a transparent window should not be resizable via dragging. As for why it worked previously, I think it was either due to a particular combination of configurations that bypassed this limitation or an incomplete implementation. Window configuration on Windows is quite fragile, and I can only make changes according to the original design intent of the code and the documentation; otherwise, it may lead to unexpected issues.
